original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Preserve the complete fixed PR3865 q-Toeplitz replay while omitting exact zero scalar products in its rational matrix multiplication.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card is narrowed to the 30-matrix PR3865 command, including all 300 complete matrix multiplications and every original check.
bottleneck_link: This is verification tooling. It reduces exact replay arithmetic without claiming a new mathematical factorization, native improvement or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop at the first complete-output-preserving arithmetic reduction and measured complete-command improvement; package it without extending the matrix domain.
evidence: The complete conformance stream compares all 4550 entries of 300 matrix products. Exact multiplication count falls from 22050 to 6650, eliminating 15400 zero products. All original checks remain. BENCHMARK.json records 15 alternating fresh-process pairs with zero errors.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does this exact zero-product omission improve a larger currently used rational replay with comparably sparse factors?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The present standalone replay is short, so interpreter startup limits its practical gain. A larger existing replay may benefit more.
open_questions.first_step: Profile one different complete replay and enumerate its zero products before changing it.
open_questions.blocked_by: No larger workload or unmodified output-equivalence contract is established by this package.
